correctness.rationale: Unique degree-two vertex on the n-side gives the wildcard encoding; the three possible one-edge exchanges on each square are exhaustively identified. A constructive path achieves the proposed distance and each allowed move changes its target distance by at most one. Walsh functions on fixed-wildcard slices decompose adjacency into (n−3−2r)I+2J blocks, giving spectrum, multiplicities and connectedness; sphere and Wiener sums follow binomial moments. Independently built wildcard-state BFS n=2..5 and direct spectral computations n=2..4 reproduce the results. The infinite n claim relies on the explicit proof, not sampling.

evidence: Maurer 1973 basis exchange uses all one-edge basis swaps, not only those with four-cycle fundamental circuits; Bousquet et al 2020 consider distinct leaf conditions or simultaneous square switches.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither class theorem directly forces exact restricted graph distances because deletion of longer-cycle swaps changes graph metric and spectrum.
